units.function: Integration-style tests for Claude Local environment diagnostics across host CLI and remote sandbox targets, including authentication-mode reporting, working-directory preparation, permission-safe probes, managed configuration seeding and CLI capability negotiation.
units.dependencyDirection: Company/adapter configuration and process environment feed a vendor adapter diagnostic service; local or injected remote runners execute command probes. Host Claude configuration is sanitized into a Paperclip-managed runtime directory, while selected instructions and remote credentials are materialized for the sandbox execution target.
units.keyDataModels: Structured diagnostic status/check code/level/message, adapter engine/command/cwd/env/effort, executionTarget kind/transport/providerKey/remoteCwd/runner, Anthropic API-key and Bedrock environment modes, managed CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, Claude settings/CLAUDE.md/credentials and cached CLI flag capabilities.
units.lifecycle: Diagnostics classify host or adapter authentication environment, create a missing absolute local cwd, derive remote cwd when unset, probe the CLI in a sandbox with an explicit allowed-tools argument rather than global permission bypass, sanitize host settings and credentials into managed runtime config, preserve sandbox-local credentials, seed CLAUDE.md, and downgrade unsupported effort flags to a warning while completing the hello probe.
units.testAssessment: Strong tests cover stable diagnostic codes, host/adapter auth precedence, nonfatal API-key warnings, Bedrock mode, cwd creation/defaulting, safer sandbox permission arguments, stripping dangerous host hooks/MCP/permission flags and credentials, preservation of remote credentials, instruction seeding and version-capability fallback. Missing are arbitrary-path/symlink/TOCTOU and filesystem-permission attacks, env/command allowlisting, secret redaction from diagnostics/logs/errors, credential file modes and lifecycle cleanup, hostile CLAUDE.md prompt injection, runner identity/attestation, probe timeout/cancel/retry, concurrent config materialization, network/data-egress policy, cross-company isolation and proof that diagnostics cannot mutate production state unexpectedly.
units.designRationale: Detect whether a configured local Agent can actually run in its selected environment while avoiding unattended permission prompts and preventing host-only execution settings or credentials from leaking into a remote sandbox.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Connector health and runtime-attestation checks that are safe, secret-free and deployment-profile neutral, while local enterprise execution nodes must isolate host credentials, instructions, tools and data from each Work environment.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the structured check codes, capability probing, remote-cwd abstraction, explicit probe tool policy and sanitize-then-materialize runtime-config pattern inside Connector nodes. Make diagnostics read-only by default; require a separately approved prepare action for filesystem changes, canonical workspace roots, strict env/command allowlists, secret handles rather than values, instruction provenance and injection scanning, ephemeral credentials with restrictive modes, egress policy and short-lived signed runtime attestations returned to the control plane.
units.responsibilityConflict: The diagnostic path creates a caller-selected absolute cwd and copies host CLAUDE.md content into the sandbox without an explicit responsible-human approval or recorded digest. Authentication and credentials are inferred from ambient process/adapter env, so Company-level authority and secret ownership are not proven. A successful hello probe establishes availability but not the exact runtime, tools, permissions, data contract or instructions later used for accountable Work.
